To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CaMKII‐dependent phosphorylation of SR proteins facilitates Ca2+ release from the SR in skeletal muscle.

CaMKII‐mediated phosphorylation facilitates SR release of Ca2+, and the facilitation is most pronounced in the presence of high levels of SR‐bound Ca2+, as is the case during repetitive tetanic stimulation.
CaMKII‐mediated phosphorylation facilitates SR calcium release in mouse skeletal muscles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca2+ in skeletal muscle.
the role of calmodulin kinase in the control of skeletal muscle contraction.
the regulation of the Ca2+ release channel in skeletal muscle, which is responsible for the activation of contraction.

CaMKII‐dependent phosphorylation of SR Ca2+, release‐related proteins is required for normal function of the contractile apparatus in skeletal muscle.
